profile.note: Identical to the 008-a P2 profile (frozen structural policy).

candidate_rule.statement: A Text event is candidate prose iff its open-tag ancestor set intersects PROSE_CONTAINERS and does not intersect NON_PROSE_CONTAINERS, with the two 008-a implementation rules carried unchanged into the runtime: D1 token-family matching and the D0 autolink-destination rule.
candidate_rule.d1_token_family_matching: A family entry matches its own token or any level-suffixed token of the form '<entry>:<suffix>' (e.g. S.Head matches S.Head:1..S.Head:6; S.List:ol:2 matches no entry). Carried unchanged from the 008-a evaluator.
candidate_rule.d0_autolink_destination: The only S.Link whose original source slice starts with byte '<' is a CommonMark autolink; its inner Text leaf is the link destination and is PROTECTED. Deterministic source-byte test, no content parsing. Codifies the 008-a documented D0 evaluator rule (finding B resolution).

policy_decisions.rationale: Open 008-a policy item resolved: these wrap prose, not machine content; the mechanism (ancestors via the enclosing prose container) already exposes them and that behaviour is now the intended policy.
Open 008-a policy item resolved: conservative default; revisit only with future evidence.

residual_layer.scope: A narrow content-level recognizer operating ONLY on parser-approved candidate-prose spans, in code-point coordinates. It must NOT reparse Markdown structure, code, parser-recognized math, HTML, or metadata, and must not contain Markdown-delimiter regexes (it is not a second Markdown parser).

classes.description: \( ... \) inline TeX: pair without newline, nonempty, span <= 200 code points; unpaired '\'(' with math-like remainder to end of span (<= 200 cp) is also protected.
\[ ... \] display TeX: pair, span <= 500 code points (may span lines); unpaired '\'[' with math-like remainder to end of span (<= 500 cp) is also protected.

Selected TeX environments: begin/end pairs for equation, equation*, align, align*, aligned, gather, gather*, gathered, eqnarray, matrix, pmatrix, bmatrix, vmatrix, cases, split; span <= 1000 code points; unbalanced begin (no matching end) protects begin-to-end-of-span for the same bound.

Bare JSON: maximal run starting at '{' or '[' that is JSON-like (balanced or truncated), no Markdown structure, <= 2000 code points; balanced pairs protected, truncated (unbalanced) protects to end of the containing prose span line.

YAML/TOML/INI/config-like text: (v2, unchanged) runs of >= 2 consecutive 'key: value' / 'key = value' style lines, or a '[section]' header followed by such lines; (v3 extension, strictness contract 008-g 4(a)(1)) a single key-value style line with a word key (letter/underscore start) is protected only when the whole trimmed value is machine-like (a number with optional short unit, a path, a relative path, an identifier, an environment-variable form, or a single-line quoted literal) or the line is part of a >= 2-line structural run; a single key line with an empty value is protected when it is immediately followed by >= 1 nested list-style line (dash-plus-space continuation); nested list-style lines extend a protected key-value run. Line-level trigger; <= 2000 code points per new single-line protection (carried-over runs keep the v2 implementation behaviour). Parser-split form (recorded D0 classification, see malformed_class_map 'yaml-nested-parser-split'): when the dialect separates an empty-value key line from its nested list continuation into different blocks, the key line is policy-exposed (the layer cannot protect across block boundaries).

HTML/XML tag fragments the parser dialect does not recognize as HTML (scope 008-g 4(a)(2)); the residual layer only sees parser-approved candidate-prose text, and the class fires only on tag names the pinned pulldown-cmark 0.13.4 dialect does NOT recognize as inline HTML - namespaced prefix-colon names (with attributes, so the autolink path does not claim them) or names outside the dialect's recognized tag-name shape [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9-]* (period/underscore names); recognized tag names abstain, so recognised-HTML behaviour stays byte-identical to v2): a paired fragment from an angle-bracket opening tag to its matching closing tag (same case-sensitive name) or self-closing marker is protected in full; an unbalanced opening fragment is protected to the end of its line (recorded 008-g D0 choice: protected, not policy-exposed); a standalone closing tag token is protected as a machine fragment. Span bound <= 2000 code points. The class must NOT fire on angle brackets used as comparison operators or followed by digits (inequality, 'less than N' forms) and must NOT fire on a lone angle bracket (trigger requires a letter/underscore after '<' and a closing '>' on the same line) (008-i D1-5, order scope item 4, PRIMARY branch committed under the EXTEND-IF-EVIDENCED gate): the class ADDITIONALLY fires when the tag name IS in the dialect vocabulary but the tag as a whole fails the dialect's inline-HTML recognition SOLELY because of a non-ASCII attribute name (dialect ground truth, pulldown-cmark 0.13.4: an attribute name's first char must be ASCII alpha/_/: and its remaining chars ASCII alnum/_.:-; a non-ASCII character anywhere in an attribute-name position makes the whole tag unrecognised, while non-ASCII in attribute VALUES does not) - in that case the opening-tag token (for an opening tag) or the standalone closing-tag token (for a closing tag) is protected as a machine fragment. The refinement is gated to that exact measured condition (v3 evidence: the two 30 B structured-xml documents, byte split 18+10+2, REPORT-008H.md section 6), preserves the vocabulary abstention for ASCII-attribute tags (v2 parity), and adds no residual-grammar growth beyond the predeclared single trigger condition

Shell/terminal commands and flags: a line starting with a shell prompt ('$ ', '# ', '> ') or a bounded command vocabulary (sudo python python3 uv git curl npm npx pip pipx pytest ruff mypy cargo make gcc g++ cc rustc ls cat grep awk sed echo export cd mv cp rm mkdir touch tar zip) followed by arguments; command-line flag tokens (--word, -single-letter) and their attached values; whole affected line(s) protected.
POSIX paths (rooted '/' with >= 1 segment, or relative a/b with >= 2 path segments and a dotless final segment) and Windows paths (drive ':' + backslash/slash, or UNC \\host\share).
Environment variables: '${NAME}' or '$NAME' where NAME is [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]* and (NAME contains '_' or NAME is all-uppercase with >= 2 chars).

Identifiers: underscored identifiers or identifiers containing a digit, [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]* (carried semantics of the 008-a legacy _IDENTIFIER rule), plus ALL_CAPS identifiers of >= 2 letters with no digit-only runs (carried semantics of _UPPER_IDENTIFIER).

Machine-significant numbers with short units: signed decimal numbers (., or , decimals) with an optional immediately-adjacent short unit (1-8 letters or %); carried semantics of the 008-a legacy _NUMBER rule.
Bare URLs missed by the parser dialect: http:// or https:// (case-insensitive) followed by a non-space, non-'<' run; carried semantics of the 008-a legacy _URL rule.

residual_layer.excluded_from_residual: Markdown delimiters (backticks, brackets/parens as link syntax, #, *, -, ~, |), code, parser-recognized math, HTML, metadata, and list/heading markers are NOT residual classes; exposure of bare delimiters is neutral by policy (see malformed class map).

coordinate_contract.unit: code-point coordinates into the unmodified original for all public intervals; byte coordinates only at the parser protocol boundary
invariants: 0 <= s <= e for every interval; intervals lie in [0, len(text)]
every parser byte range lies on UTF-8 code-point boundaries (no bisection)
original_bytes[start_byte:end_byte) is the exact intended source slice
byte<->code-point mapping is deterministic and exactly reversible
coordinate_contract.fail_closed: Any bounds or UTF-8 boundary failure is rejected fail-closed (legacy fallback), never repaired by guessing.

triggers: helper unavailable or not a regular file
helper stdout not valid UTF-8 JSONL
protocol event out of order or unbalanced
fail_closed_fallback.behaviour: legacy full-regex protection (the 008-a protected.py rule set, code-point coordinates) with the fallback reason recorded in the result; never fail open (an unprotected result is never returned)
fail_closed_fallback.legacy_rules: fenced-code, inline-code, markdown-link, url, path, relative-path, shell, number, identifier, upper-identifier, structured, tool-argument

determinism: Identical input bytes -> identical protected-interval bytes (helper is deterministic for pinned pulldown-cmark 0.13.4; residual recognizers are pure functions of the candidate-prose text).

helper.protocol: one JSON line per event {"i":<idx>,"k":"<kind token>","s":<start_byte>,"e":<end_byte>} followed by {"eof":true}

malformed_class_map.note: Frozen per-malformed-class expected outcome for the dev-corpus safety metric. 'protected' = the byte must be covered by the final protected set (structural parser interval or residual recognizer); 'policy-exposed' = policy-decided exposure, recorded but not a safety violation (008-a GO residual bound: delimiter-only residue is a bounded second-stage abstention, not a failure).

unclosed-fence.mechanism: structural: pulldown-cmark extends the fenced code block to end of input.

unmatched-backtick.mechanism: a single backtick is a literal character (not a delimiter pair); backtick delimiters are outside residual authority (no Markdown-delimiter regexes). Machine sub-tokens inside (urls/paths/identifiers/numbers) are still protected by their own residual classes.

unmatched-dollar.mechanism: a lone '$' is ambiguous between currency and math; the parser does not pair it and the residual layer abstains (currency dollars must stay exposed as prose).

incomplete-display-dollar.mechanism: an unbalanced '$$' is not display math to the parser; TeX-like content between markers is not a declared residual class (only \( \[ environments are); currency interpretation remains the conservative abstention.

incomplete-paren-bracket.mechanism: residual tex-paren / tex-bracket classes cover unpaired '\(' and '\[' with math-like remainder.

unclosed-tex-env.mechanism: residual tex-env class protects an unbalanced begin to end of span.

broken-link.mechanism: the URL sub-token is protected by the residual url class; the bracket/paren delimiter residue is neutral (policy-exposed delimiter, machine content protected).

partial-html.mechanism: structural: HTML tags are Html/InlineHtml events, never Text, so tag bytes are never candidate prose.

truncated-json.mechanism: residual bare-json class protects the truncated JSON run.

malformed-nesting.mechanism: unbalanced Markdown emphasis delimiters are literal text/delimiters; prose inside remains prose; no residual class owns Markdown delimiters.

mid-document-yaml.mechanism: residual yaml-toml-config extended class (v3): strict single-line word-key machine-like key-value, carried-over >= 2-line runs and section runs, nested list-style continuation; the v1 hidden defect shapes (single-line, nested, sectionless mid-document YAML) are the named acceptance targets on the v2 set.

mid-document-xml-fragment.mechanism: residual xml-fragment class (v3): non-recognized tag fragments (namespaced prefix-colon names, non-block-start tags, self-closing, paired, unbalanced) protect paired fragments in full, unbalanced opening fragments to end of line, standalone closing tokens in full; the v1 hidden defect shapes are the named acceptance targets on the v2 set.

yaml-nested-parser-split.mechanism: 008-g new shape, policy-decided-suppression (not a safety violation): the parser dialect separates an empty-value YAML key line from its nested list-style continuation into different blocks (the list interrupts the paragraph), so the two never share one candidate-prose context; the residual layer is a pure function of a single candidate-prose span (frozen architecture) and cannot protect across block boundaries. The exposed bytes are the key line (a word plus colon) and the list marker glue; list item words remain candidate prose. The in-context form of the v3 single-key contract (key line immediately followed by nested list lines within the same span) IS protected wherever the parser keeps the lines together (isolated spans; legacy-fallback path). Bounded second-stage abstention per the 008-a GO residual bound, mirroring the delimiter-only residue classes.

policy_exposed_dialect_ambiguity.note: Policy-exposed dialect-ambiguity classes (008-h, order scope item 3a and the 008-h D1-4 registration): shapes where the frozen pulldown-cmark dialect exposes bytes that a real LLM might intend as machine content, and where no bounded recognizer within the 2026-09-17 human-named machine-significant categories is viable (recorded reason) or the composition contract removes the shape from the v3 pool (composition contract field). Exposure under these classes is policy-decided (policy-exposed), not a safety violation: the hard safety axis is construction-labeled protected bytes (zero tolerance) on the sealed v3 set. The v2 measurement (51 B of 384,363 labeled protected bytes, 3 of 2,000 documents) remains the permanent record of the unnormalized risk magnitude.

classes.shape_rule: A structured-html closing-tag line immediately followed (no blank line) by a fenced or indented code component: the closing-tag line opens a CommonMark HTML block that absorbs the code fence and the code body up to the first internal blank line; the remaining code lines parse as paragraph text and are exposed. The v3 composition contract (R1) inserts exactly one blank line for this adjacency, so the shape cannot occur in the v3 pool; real LLM output containing the raw shape is classified by this class rather than passing as an unmeasured violation.
classes.measured_evidence: v2 hidden acceptance: 1 of 2,000 documents, 35 B of 384,363 labeled protected bytes exposed (0.0091 percent); identical under the unfixed 008-c implementation (pre-existing dialect-interaction gap, not a fix regression). Visible dev-edge batch (defect-dev-008h e01, e04): the exposed code runs after the internal blank line are labeled policy-exposed per this class and the protected runs (HTML block, second fence to end of input) are fail-closed validated. With the R1 separator (defect-dev-008h e02, e03) the fence/indented code parses as a genuine code block and is fully protected; without the separator and without an internal blank line (e31, e32) the HTML block runs to end of input and the whole tail is protected (class boundary: exposure begins at the first internal blank line).
classes.composition_contract: R1 separator (builder inserts one template-owned NEUTRAL blank line; recorded in the document composition provenance)

classes.shape_rule: A structured-keyvalue component containing a list-item-style line (list marker plus space) with paired emphasis markers or quoted emphasis-like content: the dialect parses list + strong/emphasis; the emphasis delimiters and list marker are structural (protected) but the quoted content (quote characters plus word) remains candidate prose and is exposed. The v3 composition contract (R2) admits no such component into the v3 pool; real LLM output containing the raw shape is classified by this class.
classes.measured_evidence: v2 hidden acceptance: 2 of 2,000 documents (same component), 16 B total (8 B each) of 384,363 labeled protected bytes exposed; identical under the unfixed 008-c implementation. Visible dev-edge batch (defect-dev-008h e06, e07): the quoted content is labeled policy-exposed per this class and the structural delimiters are fail-closed validated; the key line of the split form is the existing yaml-nested-parser-split class.
classes.composition_contract: R2 component admission exclusion (hash-only matching criterion and excluded count recorded in generation-identity-008h.json)

classes.shape_rule: A hash-plus-text line (a YAML comment line) at paragraph level: the dialect parses it as an ATX heading; the '# ' marker is structural (protected) and the comment text is candidate prose (exposed). A '#name' line without the space is plain prose (all exposed).
classes.recorded_reason: a hash-plus-text line is contextually indistinguishable from a Markdown ATX heading, so no bounded recognizer within the 2026-09-17 human-named machine-significant categories is viable (the residual layer must not reparse Markdown structure; treating every '# text' line as a YAML comment would require heading-vs-comment disambiguation that is a Markdown-structure decision, not a named-category content decision)
classes.measured_evidence: v1 diagnostic re-run (labeled development diagnostic, single-use spent set): 348 B (343 B + 5 B) of the 458 B v1 exposed total. Visible dev-edge batch (defect-dev-008h e08, e10): the comment text is labeled policy-exposed per this class with the '#' marker protected and the surrounding machine-like key lines protected; e09: the no-space negative stays plain prose.

classes.shape_rule: A recognized Markdown table: the table structure (row delimiters, the separator row) is structural (protected) but the cell and head text is candidate prose (exposed); the parser dialect does not treat the table as a protected unit. Table-like rows that do not form a recognized table (missing leading delimiter or separator row) parse as plain paragraph prose (all exposed except residual-class tokens).
classes.measured_evidence: 008-g naturalistic consistency aggregate (70 labeled cases, frozen labels): 9 of the 15 exposed ranges, 615 B - 8 recognized-table ranges (546 B: nat-algorithm-python-hidden-03 lines 20-23, 22 B; nat-comparison-table-hidden-02 lines 3-4, 26 B; nat-comparison-table-hidden-04 lines 3-4, 36 B; nat-json-config-hidden-01 lines 26-34, 255 B; nat-math-answer-hidden-04 lines 3-7, 53 B; nat-qa-answer-hidden-05 lines 5-6, 10 B; nat-table-equations-hidden-02 lines 3-4, 19 B; nat-table-equations-hidden-03 lines 3-7, 125 B) plus 1 unrecognized table-like range (nat-glossary-entry-hidden-03 lines 18-20, 69 B).

classes.shape_rule: List item content (S.Item) is candidate prose: machine-like content inside list items is exposed unless a bounded residual class fires within the item's prose context; the list structure itself is not a protected unit.
classes.measured_evidence: 008-g naturalistic consistency aggregate: 2 of the 15 exposed ranges, 250 B (nat-json-config-hidden-01 lines 37-40, 184 B; nat-qa-answer-hidden-04 lines 10-13, 66 B).

classes.shape_rule: Indented lines that the parser dialect reads as lazy paragraph continuation (not an indented code block, e.g. immediately after a non-blank paragraph line) expose their content as paragraph prose; code intent is a composition/authoring fact the dialect does not recover.
classes.measured_evidence: 008-g naturalistic consistency aggregate: 1 of the 15 exposed ranges, 45 B (nat-qa-answer-hidden-03 lines 15-21).

classes.shape_rule: Within a machine-significant line, the bounded residual classes protect the machine tokens (numbers, paths, identifiers) but the line's glue bytes (spaces, punctuation) remain candidate prose (exposed); the residual layer protects tokens, not whole-line glue.
classes.measured_evidence: 008-g naturalistic consistency aggregate: 3 of the 15 exposed ranges, 17 B (nat-changelog-hidden-03 line 3, 6 B; nat-changelog-hidden-03 line 10, 6 B; nat-glossary-entry-hidden-02 line 26, 5 B).

composition_contract.note: Builder-level composition contract for the v4 hidden pool (order 008-i scope item 3; implemented and asserted in research/prose-boundary/tools/prose_boundary_builder.py, the released 008-i builder). It constrains how components are composed so the v3 construction-exposure shapes cannot be composed into the v4 pool; it is not a residual class and adds no recognizer.

r1_html_block_start_barrier.rule: A fenced or indented code component is never composed on the line immediately after a dialect HTML block-start line (pulldown-cmark 0.13.4 HTML block types 1-7: closing-tag lines; opening-tag lines with continuation - a block-level tag line carrying a second tag, trailing content, or an incomplete tag; unterminated <!-- ... -->, <? ... ?>, <![CDATA[ ... ]]>, or <! + ASCII alpha lines (terminator absent on the line); pre/style/script/textarea lines); on that adjacency the builder inserts exactly one blank line (template-owned NEUTRAL delimiter).
r1_html_block_start_barrier.preserved_008h_contract: The 008-g closing-tag behaviour and the 008-h R1/R2/R3 contract otherwise stay intact, INCLUDING the 008-h test-pinned corner (byte-frozen test test_r1_not_on_non_closing_tag): a bare single COMPLETE OPENING tag at EOL (e.g. <div>, <table>) is NOT barriered - the disclosed R1 corner; its residual gap is monitored by the pre-seal diagnostic and the as-is sealing rule (disclosed in REPORT-008I.md boundary_fidelity).
r1_html_block_start_barrier.v3_evidence: v3 hidden acceptance: the 2 x 139 B html-opening-tag-adjacent-fence-absorption shape (v3h-000713, v3h-001274; family code-cpp; template T10-randomized) - the complete multi-tag opening line opens a type-6 HTML block that absorbed the code fence and first lines; the guard composes the barrier so the fence is a real code fence (dev-edge defect-dev-008i e01: 0 PROTECTED exposed bytes under the guard; the raw no-barrier variant re-derives the v3 mechanism).

display_dollar_adjacency_guard.rule: A malformed-incomplete-display-dollar component (unterminated $$ opener) is never composed immediately before a component whose first line opens a display-dollar expression (a first line of exactly $$); on that adjacency the builder inserts exactly one NEUTRAL-labeled blank line (template-owned delimiter). The barrier mechanism is the predeclared one-NEUTRAL-blank-line barrier: verified against the pinned helper that a blank line before the next $$ line makes the opener degrade to literal paragraph text, breaking the dialect's cross-pairing (no barrier substitution was needed).
display_dollar_adjacency_guard.no_new_class: NO new TeX-command residual class: the 008-g spec stays (paren/bracket/env only); a residual-grammar addition is out of scope (order scope item 3b).

t6_link_destination_admission.rule: T6-prose-link-prose link-destination fragments must be clean URLs (https?:// with no whitespace and no angle brackets); the builder asserts it at composition (machine-urls fragments first, then any other clean-URL machine fragment). The v3 pool invariant (prescan-confirmed clean machine-urls) is made explicit and builder-asserted; already-committed dev documents with non-clean T6 destinations are NOT re-labeled (dev data frozen).

d1_5_xml_fragment_class_boundary.decision: PRIMARY branch (bounded trigger refinement), committed under the predeclared EXTEND-IF-EVIDENCED gate (order 008-i Governance D1-5, scope item 4): both committed-evidence conditions held - (1) the dev regression gate showed zero NEW safety exposures on the 3,000-document dev corpus, the 008-g dev batch, and the 008-h dev-edge batch, and on the new 008-i dev-edge batch exactly the predeclared measured shape-(ii) attribution target and nothing else (run A, 008-h implementation) with zero exposures on all four sets under the refined implementation (run B); (2) the focused positive/negative tests (research/tests/test_008i_composition_and_class_boundary.py) pass - the class fires on the measured non-ASCII-attribute shape and still ABSTAINS on a non-vocabulary tag name with non-ASCII attributes (v2-parity guard preserved) and on a vocabulary name with ASCII attributes.
d1_5_xml_fragment_class_boundary.refinement: the single trigger condition _tag_non_ascii_attr_name (dialect attribute-name scan simulation) applied in the xml-fragment class's opening and standalone-closing branches: fire when the tag name is in the dialect vocabulary but the tag as a whole fails inline recognition solely because of a non-ASCII attribute name; one revertible predicate in research/curated/prose_boundary.py; nothing else in the curated file changes.
d1_5_xml_fragment_class_boundary.v3_evidence: v3 hidden acceptance, shape 2 (REPORT-008H.md section 6): 2 x 30 B (v3h-000625, v3h-001241; family structured-xml; template T10-randomized; byte split 18+10+2) - a dialect-vocabulary-name tag with a non-ASCII attribute name is neither recognised inline (its bytes become candidate prose) nor covered by the name-based class (which abstains for vocabulary names, the v2-parity guard); byte-identical under the 008-g implementation (pre-existing).
d1_5_xml_fragment_class_boundary.dev_edge: defect-dev-008i e02 (D008i-B-xml-non-ascii-attr): the measured shape under the 008-h implementation exposes exactly the 21 B tag token (interior number + identifier covered by their own classes); under the refined implementation 0 PROTECTED exposed bytes.
d1_5_xml_fragment_class_boundary.strongest_counterargument: as registered in the order Governance D1-5: refining the trigger on attribute-name shape is dialect-condition accretion; the containment is the exact-measured-condition gate, the preserved vocabulary abstention, the single revertible predicate, and the FALLBACK branch (documented boundary) had the evidence not cleanly supported the refinement.

t6_link_destination_observation.note: Measured observation (NOT a residual class, order 008-i scope item 3c): the template T6-prose-link-prose uses a machine fragment as the Markdown link destination and labels the whole region PROTECTED by construction; when the fragment is not a clean URL, the residual layer covers the machine tokens (url class) but not the inter-token space bytes, which would then be exposed. The v3 prescan confirmed the v3 pool's machine-urls are clean URLs, so the shape did NOT materialize in the v3 pool (REPORT-008H.md section 6); committed dev documents carry it as NEUTRAL-labelled oracle-split material in non-T6 templates (dev data frozen; no re-labeling). The v4 pool makes the invariant explicit via the T6 clean-URL admission (composition_contract), and the shape is retained as committed dev material in defect-dev-008i e04 with NEUTRAL-split labels (machine URL tokens PROTECTED oracle-refined via the residual url class; inter-token space NEUTRAL; no whole-region PROTECTED).

frozen_protection_identity.note: the 008-i four-file frozen protection census (008-h used v3+v4; 008-i uses v3+v5); v5 is the policy of record for this round.
